hero.lead: Centuries-old carob trees, green ceibos in the middle of the drought and ravines that reach the sea. A living territory that is best protected when visited with respect.
hero.imageAlt: Group of visitors hiking a dry forest trail among carob trees and sandy hillsides
hero.imagePlaceholder: Panoramic photo: carob and ceibo trees at sunset

explorer.lead: Schematic map of the Sullana – Máncora corridor. Tap a destination to see what to do, how to get there and who will welcome you.

angolo.name: El Angolo Hunting Reserve
angolo.desc: The heart of the dry forest: hills covered in carob, hualtaco and palo santo trees, home to the white-tailed deer and the Sechuran fox.

amotape.name: Cerros de Amotape National Park
amotape.desc: Part of the Northwest Biosphere Reserve. Dry forest that blends into Pacific tropical forest along a single route.

fernandez.name: Fernández Ravine and mud pools
fernandez.desc: A few minutes from the beach, the ravine opens onto mud pools and thermal water surrounded by dry forest.

lancones.name: Lancones Forests
lancones.desc: Hamlets in the middle of the carob grove where honey, algarrobina syrup and goat cheese are made. Borderland scenery, total silence.

poechos.name: Poechos Reservoir
poechos.desc: A large lake among dry hills. Intense sunsets, waterbirds and artisanal fishing by neighboring communities.

chira.name: Chira River Valley
chira.desc: The river that gives life to the north: farms, carob mills and towns with culinary tradition on the edge of the forest.

ecosystem.lead: The equatorial dry forest goes months without rain. When water arrives, it turns green within days. These are some of the species that sustain it.

algarrobo.name: Carob tree (Algarrobo)
algarrobo.note: Roots up to 50 m deep reach groundwater. Its fruit becomes algarrobina syrup.

ceibo.name: Ceibo
ceibo.note: A green trunk that photosynthesizes when the tree drops its leaves. Stores water inside.

palosanto.name: Palo santo
palosanto.note: Aromatic wood used for generations. Harvesting must be sustainable.

venado.name: White-tailed deer
venado.note: A symbol of El Angolo. Seen at dawn near ravines.

ardilla.name: Guayaquil squirrel
ardilla.note: Agile resident of the carob trees, easy to spot across the north.

zorro.name: Sechuran fox
zorro.note: Adapted to extreme aridity. Feeds on carob fruit.

community.lead: The families living next to the reserves care for the forest every day. Hire local guides, buy their products and sleep in their homes: every sol stays in the territory.

guides.title: Local guides
guides.text: People who know every ravine and every track. Their knowledge makes the route safe and authentic.

honey.title: Honey and algarrobina
honey.text: Forest products made by families from Lancones, Sullana and surrounding areas.

lodging.title: Community lodging
lodging.text: Sleep in community homes, share the kitchen and the country way of life.

crafts.title: Crafts
crafts.text: Textiles, ceramics and objects made from local materials, without harming the land.

green.title: The forest awakens
green.text: Rain, flowing ravines and lush foliage. Ideal for photography and birdwatching. Some roads may close.

dry.title: The golden forest
dry.text: Easier access, clear skies and wildlife concentrated near water. The best time for hikes and 4×4 routes.

visit.ctaTitle: Build your route with a community guide.
